_comment: THE NUMBERS IN THIS FILE ARE CONSERVATIVE AND UNVALIDATED.
BRIEF.md deliberately fixes no threshold, no window and no cooldown, and
CLAUDE.md rule 8 forbids inventing one and then treating it as decided.
Every value here exists so that a threshold EXISTS and is enforced; none
of them has been checked against a real listing's price series, because at
this phase this repository has never watched one for ninety days. They are
outputs of living with the system: change them deliberately, in a commit
that says why, and expect the first change to be the one that comes after
the first alert that was not worth having.
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored by the
loader. Every other key is required: nothing here has a built-in default
and the process refuses to start on a file that is missing one.
_sourceId: The source id the delivery channel spends against in config/governor.json.
The governor's second gate refuses a source it has never heard of, so this
name must appear under 'sources' there. It is NOT a retailer: nothing is
collected under it, and it exists so that notification traffic is counted,
paused and ceilinged like every other request this system makes.

_comment: One entry per rule instance. `window-low` is the only kind this build
implements: is this observation the lowest price inside its window, by at
least a margin? The roadmap phase orders it first because it is
deterministic against stored numbers; the tuned rules (a percentage drop
against a rolling reference, seasonal buying windows, per-category
thresholds) are a later phase and are not configurable here yet.
windowMs               how far back the comparison looks, from the
observation's own instant.
minimumObservations    how many observations must be inside that window
before the rule is evaluated at all. This is the
number that stops a listing added yesterday
declaring an all-time low today.
improvementMinorUnits  how much lower than the window's low the
observation must be, in the currency's own minor
units. Integer, because a percentage of an exact
integer is where the first float on this path
would come from. 100 is one dollar in USD; it is
one hundred yen in JPY, so a household watching
more than one currency wants a rule per currency.
cooldownMs             how long this rule stays quiet for a listing
after it has fired for it.
Ninety days is the shortest of the windows BRIEF.md section 4
mentions ('all-time/365-day/90-day lows'), so it is the one that can
say anything at all in this system's first season. Twelve observations
in ninety days is a listing that has been watched for a while and not
one added last week. One currency unit of improvement stops a one-cent
wobble around a stable price from being an alert.
EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and this system asserts no pattern for any retailer.
BRIEF.md section 4: a retailer's clearance price-ending ladder 'is
community lore that is widely reported unreliable in 2026, so endings
should only ever be a weak corroborating tag, never a trigger on their
own'. Writing one in here would be stating a fact this project does not
have. An owner who trusts an ending adds it themselves, per source, as
digits matched against the end of the exact minor-unit amount:
"bestbuy-api": ["97", "96"]
and it will still never trigger an alert on its own - it is attached to
a notification some rule already fired.
NO ENDPOINT IS CONFIGURED, so this system delivers nothing. That is the
fail-closed default and not an oversight: BRIEF.md section 9 leaves the
notification channel open, so choosing one is the owner's act and not
this repository's.
To turn alerts on: set endpoint to the absolute URL the channel
publishes to, add that host to 'hosts' in config/governor.json (a host
with no ceiling is refused by the governor's first gate), and run
`pnpm run alerts:start-check`, which checks exactly that before anything
is sent.
The alert body is the request body; titleHeader and linkHeader name the
headers a one-line title and the listing link travel in, where the
channel has them, and are null where it does not. The credential is
read from an environment VARIABLE - never from this file - in the same
pattern config/sources.json uses, and travels in the header named here.
A worked example, for a self-hosted ntfy server (whose publish
documentation the spec for this phase carries as reference material, and
which is reference material and not a requirement):
"endpoint": "https://ntfy.example.lan/deals",
"method": "POST",
"titleHeader": "X-Title",
"linkHeader": "X-Click",
"credential": { "variable": "DEAL_SENTINEL_ALERT_TOKEN",
"header": "Authorization", "prefix": "Bearer " }
Anything that accepts a plain-text body over http works the same way;
nothing in this system is specific to one vendor.
